title: Integrated wheeled drum rover with rear high-lift hopper dump
problem_restatement: Drive over loose BP-1 simulant, excavate with low force, operate with no line-of-sight by remote link, and carry and high-lift dump regolith within 60 kg and 1.0 by 0.5 by 0.5 m start envelope.
mechanism_sentence: Big spiky wheels roll over loose soil while a spinning front drum scoops soil into a bucket that is lifted about 1 m to pour into a bin, steered by video from a tall folding mast that stops the machine if the signal is lost.
decisive_choices: Front transverse single drum with 30 mm shallow cut for low 39 N reaction instead of drag blade or deep cut
Rear high-lift mast with 0.15 m dual actuators through 4-to-1 chain at 0.80 efficiency to reach 1.05 m pour lip with 0.30 m overhang
Purchasable 24 V 20 Ah LiFePO4 pack for 480 Wh at 90.6 Wh per kg giving 53.0 kg total instead of 1000 Wh in 2.92 kg claim
open_question: Does the rear mast lift to the 1.05 m pour lip with 0.30 m overhang stay nose-down and within actuator force once deployed geometry and friction are proven by dimensioned sketch and static calculation?
transfer_line: Load: Hopper -> Rear lift mast -> Wheels | Measured: IMU -> Onboard computer

assumed_constraints.constraint: Total mass must stay under 60 kg limit
Stowed fit must stay inside 1.0 by 0.5 by 0.5 m start box
assumed_constraints.source: dimensioned stowed sketch E44 and stowed-plus-deployed sketch E48

assumed_constraints.constraint: Hopper must pour at 1.05 m lip from 0.45 m stowed pivot on 0.60 m guide
Sortie is 0.5 h at about 341 W needing about 171 Wh
assumed_constraints.source: sortie-energy calc E32 and runtime calc E36

assumed_constraints.constraint: Ground is Black Point 1 simulant with high friction and negligible cohesion
assumed_constraints.source: friction source E1 and density source E2

functional_decomposition: Drive over loose BP-1 simulant bed without excessive sinkage or slip, and climb out of dig pile
Excavate BP-1 simulant with low cutting force and load into hopper
Operate with no line-of-sight via remote link with sensing, onboard compute, and heartbeat stop-and-hold
Carry regolith in hopper and high-lift dump into collection bin within mass and start envelope

concept.working_principle: Four 300 mm grouser wheels carry a frame with front 200 mm transverse drum taking 30 mm cuts into a central hopper, folding mast carries FPV cameras plus depth and IMU from 0.45 m stowed to about 1.0 m eye with heartbeat stop-hold, and rear mast raises the hopper on a 0.60 m guide from 0.45 m pivot to 1.05 m pour lip by 0.15 m dual actuators through 4-to-1 chain at 0.80 efficiency, powered by a 24 V 480 Wh pack for a 171 Wh half-hour sortie at 53.0 kg total.

fabrication_steps.description: Assemble the frame and mount the four 300 mm wheels with traction bars
Mount the front spinning drum and the central bucket on the rear lifting mast
Mount the folding mast and fit the cameras and sensors on top
Fit the battery pack and sealed electronics box under the frame

risks.risk: Single drum 39 N reaction slips wheels or raises power
risks.mitigation: Keep cut shallow near 30 mm and hopper load centred

risks.risk: Raised 15 kg load tips over rear axle due to moment-arm sensitivity
risks.mitigation: Fix overhang at 0.30 m and wheelbase at 0.70 m and verify by deployed side sketch to 1.05 m

risks.risk: Sortie energy and pack mass do not close under limit
risks.mitigation: Use purchasable 480 Wh pack for 1.41 h margin and re-sum mass

novelty_claim: Combination of front transverse drum with central hopper on rear high-lift mast plus folding 1.0 m perception mast with heartbeat stop-hold in 60 kg wheeled rover

open_questions: Does the rear mast lift to the 1.05 m pour lip with 0.30 m overhang stay nose-down and within actuator force once deployed geometry and friction are proven by dimensioned sketch and static calculation?
